note: Two roots per context-card page, five previews on each side. context-card: the open card's floating layer, a client-only state the sketches (tools/geist/sketch/context-card.*.json) render on the mirror and the census page opens through the prepare script — the reference shows the card open in previews 4 and 5 only, so ours pins exactly those eight. context-card-trigger: the wrapper around the slotted content, present on all seventeen cards, read on `.trigger`. Run each side with theme light and dark; width fixes every preview at the mirror's 600px stage. The card's own box is moved and sized by inline styles on both sides, so its position is not compared; the text-bearing parts are read as soft. The card's width and height are set inline from the measured content, so they follow the text in our font: `card` and `fade` are named as text parts, like `box` and `body`. Both sides must be read at the SAME viewport — the layer is fixed to the viewport, so its width is the window's; the mirror pane defaults narrow, and reading it at 426px against ours at 1367px reported 208 differences that were only the window size. Resize both to 1367x924 before running.
